The polar curve $r=5$ and the ray $\theta =\frac{\pi }{3}$ intersect at the point $Q,$ as shown above. The Cartesian coordinates of $Q$ are$\,(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
worked_solution:
The polar coordinates of $Q$ are $(r,\theta )=(5,\frac{\pi }{3}).$ We can convert the polar coordinates of $Q$ to Cartesian coordinates, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =2.5 \\ y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $Q$ are $(\frac{5}{2},\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}).$
